maría: quick heads-up from evals: reproducible drop when combining gptq+fp8 with prefix KV + continuous batching

maría: numbers: throughput +17%, median token latency down ~10ms, but ROUGE-L drops ~1.6pp on our summarization suite and short-answer hallucination jumps from 0.5% -> 2.1%

maría: repro (summary): run perf-harness --model=llama-13b-v2 --quant=gptq+fp8 --cache=prefix --batch_window_ms=10 --batching=continuous --requests=40k. sample metrics in logs:
``
kv_hit=0.71
median_token_latency=36ms
rouge_l=0.369  # baseline 0.385
hallucination_rate=2.1%
```

raj: do we see this across other quant backends (awq, gptq-hybrid) or only gptq+fp8? what's prompt length distro?

maría: mostly shows up on short prompts (<48 tokens). awq reduces delta but still +0.4pp. If I disable prefix cache for short requests rouge returns to baseline.

casey: hypothesis: FP8 quant scaling state differs slightly across fused kernels. When cached KV fragments (from earlier requests) are reused for a request that had a different normalization state, tiny numerical drift is amplified in short completions. continuous batching increases the chance of mixing caches between merged requests.

emma: can you paste the cache key derivation we use? if key doesn't include quant/schema metadata we can get wrong reuse.

maría: current key snippet: 
``
key = sha256(model + version + prefix_tokens_sha)
# no quant or kernel id in key
```

raj: jeez that's the culprit. add quant_schema_id + kernel_variant + batch_window to the key. Also add seq_scale_hash (derived from layer norm scales) to be safe.

casey: operational mitigation until we roll fix: reduce continuous batch_window to 5-6ms for fp8-gptq variants and set per-model short-prefix cache TTL=8s. schedule canary.

emma: i'll put up an A/B: tiny-window + key-change in canary vs just key-change. want to capture latency and rouge tradeoffs. @deploy-bot canary?

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled on prod-dedicated-pool-2 at 2026-04-03T02:30:00Z — 5% traffic. health checks: latency, kv_hit_rate, rouge-l (eval endpoints).

maría: after landing quick patch + window reduce: kv_hit down ~5pt, median latency +4ms, rouge-l within 0.1pp of baseline. uploading traces: s3://redwood-evals/1779999999/trace/

raj: followups: (1) include quant_schema_id, kernel_variant, seq_scale_hash and batch_window in cache key; (2) instrument time spent normalizing scales and any kernel detune; (3) short-lived per-request tag to prevent reuse when batch merge occurs.

casey: i'll open PR with cache-key change + unit tests + small e2e harness reproducer. will also add feature-flag to control batching-window per-model.

maría: i'll re-run full eval sweep once PR hits canary and paste final numbers here. quick thread but good catch :thumbsup:
